representative_tasks.task: Which model should I use for my dataset? (no details given)
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Asks about task type, data size, feature types and constraints, or states assumptions before recommending

representative_tasks.task: Compare a few classifiers on a tabular dataset
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Baseline plus candidates ranked by cross-validated score

representative_tasks.task: Ship the top of a model ranking that contains nan CV scores
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Refuses: nan means failed fits/scoring, the nan sort is arbitrary; check finiteness, fix the cause, never ship the dummy baseline

negative_cases: Request to pick the model with the best training-set accuracy (planned)
rubric: Non-finite CV scores stop the comparison instead of silently changing the winner
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Ranking step that raises on non-finite CV scores and on a baseline winner
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
